59	  stands on. Pins advance only at integrate (§8).
60	- `depends:` is the merge order (§8).

64	
65	A branch here always means a git branch in a code repo. For a spec

71	  flight apart by folder (`changes/<id>/`), not by branch. That is why a
72	  change's project-level tests wait in its folder until integrate.
73	- Lead: at the go, for each code repo the spec names, and only those, make
74	  exactly one code branch, `change/<id>`, from that repo's pin in
75	  `pod.yaml`, and push it to the repo's remote.

82	    `<checkout>` a checkout of that repo whose `origin` is its remote in
83	    `pod.yaml`, and `<pin>` its full pin, and wait until they have run:
84

86	    git -C <checkout> branch change/<id> <pin>
87	    git -C <checkout> push origin change/<id>

92	  recording each base commit:
93	  `go by <handle>; branches change/<id>: <repo> <sha7>[, <repo> <sha7>]`.

109	## 2 Stages and states
110	
111	The process runs five stages, in order:
112	
113	| Stage | Role | Reads | Writes | Done when | Gate |
114	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
115	| **spec** | spec, with the human | the request, the code, earlier specs it touches | `spec.md` | every requirement has a scenario; the human approved | human approves |
116	| **plan** | plan | the approved spec, the code | `plan.md` | every requirement traces to a build task and every scenario to a test; self-review passes | human skims (project size) |

118	| **verify** | test; review | spec, project-level tests, the commit set | evidence, whole-change review | every project-level test, unit suite and declared quality check passes at the commit set; no open Critical or Important finding | none |

120	
121	A commit set is one commit per affected code repo plus the Project Space
122	commit. It is what verify runs against.
123	
124	- Lead: dispatch no plan, build or test task for a change whose spec has no
125	  `approved:` line. Given "go" on such a change, dispatch nothing and say,
126	  exactly:
127	  `Not dispatched: the spec at changes/<id>/spec.md awaits approval.`
128	- Writing the project-level tests is a test task that starts at the go, in
129	  parallel with build, from the spec alone. Builders add to those tests only
130	  by suggesting tests, which the test agent takes up or declines (§6).
131	- Read a change's state from its records. Never set it by hand.
132	
133	| State | Read from |
134	|---|---|
135	| proposed | `spec.md` exists without `approved:` |
136	| approved | `spec.md` has `approved:` |
137	| planned | `plan.md` exists with its self-review filled in |

143	## 3 Spec
144	
145	You are the spec author, and you work with the human. Describe the work to be
146	done and nothing else. A spec covers its own change only. No spec of existing
147	behavior is a precondition: a project starts with its first change, and its
148	first spec covers only that change. Only you edit a spec, and only the human
149	approves one.
150	
151	### Draw out intent
152	
153	- Look before asking. Read the code and any earlier spec the request touches
154	  until you can say how things work today. Never ask what the project already
155	  answers.
156	- Play the request back in your own words, with anything you found that
157	  bears on it: a constraint, a conflict, a cheaper path.
158	- Ask one question per message, the one whose answer most changes what gets
159	  built. Use plain words, not process jargon.
160	- Before writing up, give the two or three real ways to do it, what each
161	  trades off, and a recommendation. The human picks.
162	- List any default you fill in under Open calls. Never present it as agreed.
163	  "Just draft it" means draft now, with the defaults listed.
164	
165	### Write the spec
166	
167	Write `changes/<id>/spec.md` from `templates/records/spec.md`. The id is
168	verb-led kebab-case, such as `add-vqls-backend`.
169	
170	- Title line: `# <id>: <the intent, in one sentence>`.
171	- Header lines: `- size:` (§9), `- owner: <handle>`, `- repos: [...]` (the
172	  code repos the change touches), and `- supersedes: []` (earlier
173	  requirement ids this work changes). Later lines record the change's
174	  life: `- approved: <handle> <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ>`,
175	  `- integrated: <handle> <UTC>` and `- abandoned: <UTC> <reason>`.
176	- Sections, in this order: Why; Scope, with In and Out; Requirements;
177	  Quality; Approaches (the two or three considered, the one picked, and
178	  why); Open calls (the defaults you chose, which the human checks).
179	
180	A requirement and its scenarios, and a quality check, look like this (values
181	illustrative):
182	
183	```markdown
184	### R1 VQLS linear solver option
185	The solver SHALL accept VQLS as its linear-solver backend.
186	
187	#### R1.S1 Converges on the subsonic reference case
188	- GIVEN the quasi-1D nozzle reference case at nelem 5
189	- WHEN it is solved with the VQLS backend for 20 iterations
190	- THEN the L2 density error against the exact isentropic solution is below
191	  1e-3 (dimensionless, normalized by inlet density)
192	
193	#### R1.S2 Rejects an unknown ansatz name
194	- GIVEN an ansatz name the backend does not define
195	- WHEN the solver starts
196	- THEN it exits non-zero before building any circuit and names the bad value
197	
198	### Q1 Linter clean
199	The changed code SHALL pass the repo's linter with the repo's configuration.
200	- check: the linter's command in each affected repo; passing is exit status 0
201	```
202	
203	### Requirements and scenarios
204	
205	- One behavior per requirement, with one SHALL or MUST.
206	- Observable: someone who has never seen the code can tell whether it holds.
207	- No internals: no class names, library choices or steps.
208	- At least one scenario per requirement, exercising it, not restating it.
209	- Cover error and edge cases, not only the happy path.
210	- Every number carries its unit and tolerance, and any convention it depends
211	  on: norm, normalization, reference solution.
212	- Ids are local to the spec (`R1`, `R1.S1`) and qualified outside it
213	  (`add-vqls-backend/R1.S1`). When later work changes behavior an integrated
214	  spec requires, list those qualified ids under `supersedes`; the plan then
215	  has a test task that updates the old tests in `tests/`.
216	- A fix that restores behavior an integrated spec already requires may cite
217	  that requirement in place of new ones: a five-line spec.
218	- **Quality checks** go in the Quality section, one per tool or review: what
219	  is run, on what, and what passing means. They are requirements like any
220	  other, so verify runs them and evidence records them. Reuse a check an
221	  earlier spec declared by citing its qualified id. A spec with no Quality
222	  section asks for none.
223	
224	### Human review and approval
225	
226	Ask the human to read `Why` and `Scope` (is this the problem I meant?), then
227	`Requirements` (is "done" defined right, and does the case I care about most
228	have a scenario?), then `Open calls`. The test is whether the human would be
229	content if the pod built exactly this and nothing more.
230	
231	- The human approves in any words. Record
232	  `- approved: <handle> <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ>` with the human's handle and the
233	  UTC time.
234	- An edit to `Requirements` after approval reopens approval for that edit
235	  only. Lead: hold the tasks that serve the edited requirements, let the
236	  work that does not depend on them carry on, and record
237	  `approval reopened for <Rn>[, <Rm>]; held T<a>[, T<b>]`.
238	
239	## 4 Plan
240	
241	You are the planner. Write `changes/<id>/plan.md` from
242	`templates/records/plan.md`. The plan covers all downstream work of the
243	change: build tasks, test tasks, reviews, verify and integrate, as a
244	dependency graph. Write it for an engineer who has never seen the code or the
245	spec. It holds the decisions they cannot make alone. A plan longer than the
246	code it describes has written the code instead.
247	
248	- At project size you are a fresh agent that never saw the spec
249	  conversation. Your questions about the spec are the builder check: each is
250	  answered in the spec, decided and listed under Open calls, or sent to the
251	  human in one message, most important first.
252	- First check that every requirement has at least one scenario. If one has
253	  none, write no plan and return the spec to its author, saying exactly:
254	  `No plan written: <Rn> has no scenario. Returned to the spec author.`
255	
256	### Plan sections
257	
258	1. **Goal and approach** in two or three sentences.
259	2. **Interface contract:** the public surface the project-level tests drive:
260	   signatures with types, CLI flags, file formats, output fields, exact
261	   names. Builders build to it and testers test to it.
262	3. **Global constraints**, copied verbatim from the spec: units, tolerances,
263	   version floors, naming rules.
264	4. **File map:** per repo, the files to create or change, one responsibility
265	   each, following the repo's patterns.
266	5. **Tasks**, each in this form:
267	
268	   ```markdown
269	   ### T3 VQLS backend
270	   - role: build
271	   - repo: qutil
272	   - after: [T1]
273	   - runs: local             # local | mesh
274	   - needs: any              # environment class, or any
275	   - serves: [R1]
276	   - touches: qutil/linsolve/vqls.py, qutil/tests/test_vqls.py
277	   - consumes: LinearSolver protocol from T1
278	   - produces: VQLSSolver(ansatz: str, layers: int)
279	   - steps: failing test, watch it fail, minimal code, watch it pass, commit
280	   - done when: the unit tests in qutil/tests/test_vqls.py pass at the branch
281	     head (command and expected output given) and the task review has no
282	     Critical or Important finding
283	   ```
284	
285	   A build task is the smallest unit with its own test cycle that a
286	   reviewer could reject while approving its neighbor. Steps pin exact
287	   values and assertions. They give a function body only for an algorithm
288	   the signature and tests leave open. Build tasks run `local` for now
289	   (§11).
290	6. **Test tasks:** the project-level tests to write (role test, `after: []`,
291	   so they start at the go); a suggestions task (role test, after every
292	   build task) that takes up the builders' test suggestions, if any; and the
293	   verify run (role test, after every build and test task, with `needs:`
294	   naming the environment class the tests require), whole or in shards,
295	   each shard with its own `needs:`. A spec with entries under `supersedes`
296	   also gets a test task that updates the matching tests in `tests/`.
297	7. **Review tasks:** one per build task, plus the whole-change review after
298	   verify's first green run.
299	8. **Integrate task:** role lead, after verify and the whole-change review;
300	   it lists the docs and open plans this change touches.
301	9. **Test map:** every scenario id to its project-level test name and the
302	   task that writes it, plus any unit tests that also cover it.
303	10. **Dependency summary:** which tasks run in parallel, and the longest
304	    chain. Two tasks that touch a common file never run at the same time:
305	    make one `after` the other.
306	
307	### Parallel tasks and shards
308	
309	- Plan for parallel work. Two tasks with no dependency between them run in
310	  parallel by default. Put in a task's `after` list only the tasks whose
311	  output it needs or that touch a file it touches.
312	- A task whose work divides may be sharded: split into shards that several
313	  holders of its role run in parallel, local and remote together. Builders
314	  take independent files; testers each run part of the suite.
315	- Name the shards. Each shard is a task entry of its own, `### T<n>a
316	  <title>`, `### T<n>b <title>`, with its own `runs:`, `needs:` and
317	  `touches:`. Fields the shards share go once, under a heading that opens
318	  with all their ids, such as `### T<n>a and T<n>b <title>`.
319	- Say how the work divides: the files each build shard touches, never a
320	  file another shard touches; or the tests, unit suites and quality checks
321	  each test shard runs, or the rule the lead follows to split them at
322	  dispatch. Between them, the shards of a verify run everything verify must
323	  give a result for (§7).
324	- Build shards run `local`, like every build task, for now (§11).
325	
326	Then come the plan's last two sections, `Self-review` and `Questions for the
327	spec`. Sort each question as (a) answered, (b) minor, with the default
328	planned, or (c) for the human.
329	
330	### Self-review
331	
332	Before handing over, check: every requirement maps to a build task; every
333	scenario maps to a test; no step says "TBD", "handle edge cases" or "add
334	tests"; names and types agree across tasks; every task has role, after, runs
335	and done-when. Fill in the self-review section with the result.
336	
337	### The go
338	
339	At project size the human skims the plan before any dispatch: every task
340	traces to a requirement, nothing reaches outside the approved scope, and no
341	task hides the real decisions. Then the human says go. At small size,
342	approving the spec is the go.
343	
344	## 5 Build
345	
346	**Lead.** For each build task, write a brief from
347	`templates/records/brief.md` at `changes/<id>/tasks/T<n>-brief.md`, dispatch
348	a fresh builder (§11), and record the base commit in the dispatch line. The
349	brief holds the plan entry verbatim, the interfaces it touches, the global
350	constraints, any ruling that bears on it, the commit set to start from, by
351	sha, and where the result goes.
352	
353	**Builder.** You work from your brief.
354	
355	- Ask first if anything in your brief is unclear. If the answer would change
356	  the result, return NEEDS_CONTEXT with the question rather than guess.
357	- Work each step test first: write the failing test, watch it fail, write
358	  the minimal code, watch it pass. Run the repo's full unit suite once
359	  before reporting.
360	- White-box tests are unit tests. Anything that depends on internals, such
361	  as an internal routine's convergence order or a branch the public surface
362	  cannot reach, you test in the code repo, in the same task.
363	- Commit to the change's one branch, `change/<id>`, with trailers
364	  `Change: <id>` and `Task: T<n>`. Stage and commit only your task's files,
365	  by path, since other builders may share the branch. Rebase on the branch
366	  before pushing, and push only to it. Never create a branch. A rebase
367	  conflict means the plan's independence claim was wrong: stop and report
368	  BLOCKED.
369	- Never write or edit a project-level test or the spec. If you believe a
370	  project-level test is wrong, leave it unchanged, report
371	  DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, and put this line in `## Concerns`:
372	  `Disputed test: <test name>; spec clause: <clause>`. The lead routes it

415	## 6 Project-level tests
416	
417	You are the test agent writing the change's project-level tests. Write them
418	from the spec, the interface contract, the global constraints and the test
419	map. Do not read implementation bodies, diffs, builder reports or build-task
420	steps. Once code exists you may use its public surface, such as `--help`
421	output or signatures.
422	
423	**Lead.** Write the test-writing brief from `templates/records/test-brief.md`.
424	It carries only what this section allows: the test task's own entry, the
425	spec's path, and the interface contract, global constraints and test map
426	copied from the plan, with the commit sets to start from. It never holds an
427	implementation body, a diff, a builder report or a build-task step.
428	
429	**Test agent:**
430	
431	- Write at least one test per scenario, named with the scenario id, such as
432	  `test_R1_S1_converges_subsonic`.
433	- Take expected values from outside the code under test: literals,
434	  hand-checked fixtures, analytical or manufactured solutions, published
435	  references.
436	- Test through the public surface against the real system. Mock only what
437	  is slow or external.
438	- Before writing a test, name the change in behavior that would make it
439	  fail. A test only an intentional decision could fail, such as a message's
440	  wording, is a change detector; test the behavior instead.
441	- Give numbers units and tolerances. Record each test's expected run time;
442	  a test over 60 s is marked heavy (§11).
443	- Put tests in `changes/<id>/tests/`. They stay there until integrate moves
444	  them into `tests/`. Never put them in a code repo.
445	
446	**Watch them fail.** Run the new tests at the base commit set first. A test
447	for added or changed behavior must fail there, for the stated reason. Record
448	each result as `T<n> at base: <test name> <fail|pass> (<reason>)[, ...]`.
449	Lead: if such a test passes at base, return it to the test agent and record
450	`T<n> returned to test: <test name> passed at base`.

452	### Test suggestions from builders
453	
454	A builder sees where the code is fragile: a near-singular input, a boundary,
455	a branch only some inputs reach. A test written from the spec alone cannot
456	see that, so a builder's report may carry suggestions. The test agent learns
457	where to look from the builder, never what the answer is.
458	
459	**Builder.** Give each suggestion an id `T<n>.TS<k>` and two parts:
460	
461	```markdown
462	### T3.TS1 High CFL near the stability limit
463	- for the tester: R1 is at risk on the reference case at nelem 5 with the CFL
464	  number raised to 0.9; the solve may stall above the 1e-3 error bound
465	  without reporting an error
466	- for the reviewer: qutil/linsolve/vqls.py:120-148, where the cost function
467	  flattens as the condition number grows
468	```
469	
470	- Write the "for the tester" part in spec terms: the requirement or scenario
471	  at risk, the input, and the failure you expect. It holds no code, no diff,
472	  and no expected value the code computed.
473	- Write the "for the reviewer" part as a code location.
474	
475	**Lead.** Route each suggestion and record where it went, as
476	`T<n>.TS<k> -> <test|spec|builder>`:
477	
478	| Suggestion | Goes to | Outcome |
479	|---|---|---|
480	| Behavior the spec covers, on an input no scenario exercises | the test agent, with the "for the tester" part only | a project-level test whose expected value comes from the spec; or declined, with a reason |
481	| Behavior the spec does not state | the spec author, as a proposed scenario | approved by the human and then tested; or dropped |
482	| Internal only, nothing observable | back to the builder | a unit test in the code repo |
483	
484	- If a "for the tester" part gives an expected value the code computed,
485	  return it to the builder to restate, send nothing to the test agent, and
486	  record `T<n>.TS<k> returned to builder: carries a computed value`.
487	- Send the "for the reviewer" part to the task review and the whole-change
488	  review, which check that the builder's unit tests cover it. The test agent
489	  never sees it.
490	- Record each outcome as:
491	
492	  ```
493	  T<n>.TS<k> outcome: <tested <test name>|proposed as scenario|unit-tested|declined: <reason>|dropped>
494	  ```
495	
496	  The final report lists every suggestion and its outcome (§8).

499	
500	You are the test agent running verify. When the build tasks are done, or at
501	a checkpoint the lead picks, run at the commit set and in the environment
502	class the task names:
503	
504	- the change's project-level tests and the space's regression suite
505	  `tests/`;
506	- each affected repo's unit tests;
507	- every quality check in the spec's Quality section.
508	
509	A repo in `pod.yaml` that the spec does not name is used at its pin.
510	
511	Return an evidence record, `changes/<id>/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>.md`, from
512	`templates/records/evidence.md`:
513	
514	```yaml
515	---
516	id: ev-20261102T1412Z
517	change: add-vqls-backend
518	commit_set: {space: 5c02e1a, qutil: 77b01d4, fvm: 3f9c2ab}
519	env: linux-server

538	  - `<change>`: for a test in `tests/<change>/`, that folder's name. For a

541	    whose final report's `## Scenarios` table has such a row; where several
542	    do, the one whose archive folder name sorts last. With neither, the
543	    change of a `scenario:` value that is one id written `<change>/<value>`.

546	    test's `scenario:` front-matter value, less any `<change>/` part, when
547	    that value is exactly one id. When it is not (it lists several ids, or
548	    the test has none), the id its file name carries:
549	    `test_R<n>_S<m>_<slug>` gives `R<n>.S<m>`, `test_I<n>_<slug>` gives

558	- Put failure summaries in the body. Logs appear only as pointers:
559	  space-relative paths or URLs, never a machine path.

563	**Lead.** Route each failure:
564	
565	| Failure | Goes to | Carrying |
566	|---|---|---|
567	| Test agrees with the spec, code does not | a builder, as a fix task | scenario id, failing output |
568	| A builder says the test is wrong | the test agent, who re-derives the expectation from the spec and fixes the test or keeps it with a reason | the spec clause |
569	| Spec ambiguous, intent settles it | the lead, as a ruling | the clause and the reading chosen |
570	| Spec ambiguous or wrong, only the human can say | the human, through the spec author | a proposed edit to the spec |
571	| Flaky or environmental | the test agent, debugging per §13 | the runs that disagree |

573	**Whole-change review.** After the first green run (for a sharded verify,
574	the first time its shards' records are green together, below), dispatch a

576	change: the spec, the plan, every repo's diff, the latest evidence, and the
577	ledger's deferred minors and rulings. It checks completeness (every
578	requirement has code and a passing test), correctness (the code does what
579	the spec means, edge cases included) and coherence (the plan's decisions
580	show in the code). It uses the review format of §5, under its own task
581	number. Its findings go to one builder in one fix wave, then one re-review.
582	The lead rules on what remains.

584	### Sharded verify
585	
586	When the plan shards verify (§4), each shard is a verify run of its own. A
587	test agent runs only the tests, unit suites and quality checks its shard's
588	brief lists, and returns one evidence record for the shard:
589	
590	- named for the shard,
591	  `changes/<id>/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<shard id>.md`, with
592	  `id: ev-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<shard id>`;
593	- with two more keys: `shard: <shard id>`, and `tests: [<test name>, ...]`,
594	  the tests that record ran;
595	- with results only for what the shard ran.
596	
597	The lead starts every shard at one commit set (§11). The current commit set
598	is each code branch's head now (a repo the spec does not name, at its pin),
599	with the shards' space commit: the commit that filed the last of the latest
600	shard briefs. A shard's latest record is at the current commit set when each
601	code repo's sha in it is that repo's current one, its space commit is the
602	shards' space commit, and neither `changes/<id>/tests/` nor `tests/` has
603	changed since that commit. Otherwise it is out of date: a repo moved, it ran
604	at another space commit, or `changes/<id>/tests/` or `tests/` changed after
605	that commit. Take each shard's latest record. The records are green
606	together only when all three hold:
607	
608	- every one of them is at the current commit set;
609	- every result in every one of them is a pass;
610	- together they give a result for every scenario, regression test, unit
611	  suite and declared quality check.
612	
613	The change is verified only when they are green together and the
614	whole-change review has no open Critical or Important finding. A shard with
615	no record yet leaves the change unverified.
616	
617	While a shard is out of date, the change is not verified; the shard runs
618	again at the current commit set. Lead:
619	
620	- If the commit set has moved since the shards' space commit, through a
621	  branch head or the tests, write every shard's brief again. Its
622	  `## Start from` names the new commit set under test, so its text changes.
623	  Dispatch every shard again as §11 says, at the new shards' space commit.
624	- If the commit set has not moved, dispatch a shard again from its brief,
625	  at the same shards' space commit. That covers a shard whose record names
626	  another commit set, and a shard whose run failed for a flaky or
627	  environmental reason.
628	- A shard that failed on the code or on a test runs again only once the
629	  fix lands, routed as the table above says. The fix moves the commit set,
630	  so every shard runs again.

632	## 8 Integrate
633	
634	You are the lead, with the human. Never integrate on evidence older than the
635	space's current pins and `tests/`.
636	
637	1. **Fresh evidence.** If `tests/` or any pin in `pod.yaml` moved since the
638	   latest evidence, a build task rebases each affected change branch onto
639	   the new `main`, and verify runs again, before any merge.
640	2. **Reconcile.** The spec must describe what the code does. If the code
641	   drifted, fix the code. If the spec was wrong and the human agrees, amend
642	   it; the amendment needs approval.
643	3. **Final report**, in chat and as `changes/<id>/report.md`, from
644	   `templates/records/final-report.md`: a table of scenario, test, result
645	   and evidence id; then every ruling made on the human's behalf with its
646	   cost if wrong (the list is exhaustive: every `Ruling:` line in the
647	   ledger); then deferred minors, every test suggestion and its outcome,
648	   open questions, and each repo's branch and head.
649	4. **Merge**, only on the human's word: merge each `change/<id>` and delete
650	   it, open a pull request, or keep the branch. Repos merge in `depends`
651	   order. Discard work only when the human asks in so many words, after you
652	   confirm.
653	5. **Update**, after the merge, in one space commit: move
654	   `changes/<id>/tests/` into `tests/`, as the folder `tests/<id>/`;
655	   advance every affected pin; mark
656	   `integrated:` on the spec; move the folder to
657	   `changes/archive/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<id>/`. Docs that ship with the code are
658	   updated by a build task before the merge; project docs in the space
659	   (README, decisions) are updated by you here. Give each open plan that
660	   depended on this change a ledger line naming what moved.
661	6. **Prune** what can be regenerated, such as diff files made for review.

680	## 10 Roles
681	
682	Each pod role is held by an agent, local or on the mesh, where the role is
683	`swe.<role>`. Stay in your lane:
684	
685	| Role | Writes | Never |
686	|---|---|---|
687	| **human** | approvals, merges | needs a command |
688	| **spec** | `spec.md` | writes code or tests |
689	| **plan** | `plan.md` | edits the spec, code or tests |
690	| **lead** | ledger, briefs, rulings, final report; creates each `change/<id>` branch at the go; files every record of the change through the space's librarian | writes code, tests or the spec |
691	| **build** | code, unit tests (white-box included), shipped docs, on `change/<id>`; test suggestions in its report | writes project-level tests or the spec; reviews its own work; creates a branch |
692	| **test** | project-level tests, evidence | writes code or the spec; reads implementation bodies, diffs or builder reports while writing tests |
693	| **review** | review records | changes what it reviews; trusts a report over the diff |
694	
695	**Independence.** These must be different agents: test and build, test and
696	spec, review and build, and spec and plan at project size. A different agent
697	means at least a fresh context started from a brief, never another agent's
698	session. Where a mistake would be costly, use a different model or node too,
699	so blind spots are not shared. One node may hold several roles if each task
700	runs as its own agent.
701	
702	**Placement.**
703	
704	| Role | Usually |
705	|---|---|
706	| spec, lead | local, with the human |
707	| plan | local, or remote at project size |
708	| build | local or remote; several at once when the plan allows |
709	| test | remote, on a node of the environment class the checks need; tests are heavy |
710	| review | anywhere, on the most capable model available for the whole-change review |
711	
712	Remote build waits on the executor git exception (§11); until then, build
713	runs local.
714	
715	**Single seat.** Without a mesh, one interactive session is spec author,
716	planner, lead and the space's librarian, and dispatches fresh local subagents

718	subagent too, since spec and plan must be different agents. Without a mesh,
719	file every record through agent-mesh's `space-librarian` skill. It applies
720	the same profile, reference and id checks a mesh librarian applies (§12) and

722	core, lore or remote agent. The records are the same either way, so a
723	project can move between single-seat and mesh use at any stage boundary.

726	
727	You are the lead. Dispatch every task from the same brief,
728	`changes/<id>/tasks/T<n>-brief.md`, whatever runs it (§5, §6). The brief
729	holds the task text, the interfaces it touches, the global constraints, any
730	ruling that bears on it, the commit set to start from, and where the result
731	goes. Machine paths never go in a brief. Each role's definition is
732	`agents/swe-<role>.md` in the swe-pod product.
733	
734	- **`runs: local`.** Start a fresh subagent on your own node, of type
735	  `swe-<role>`. Its prompt holds the brief's space-relative path and, on its
736	  own line, the checkout paths on this node. Before the role definitions are
737	  installed, start a general-purpose subagent and put the definition's text
738	  above the same prompt. The agent writes its outputs at their final
739	  space-relative paths.
740	- **`runs: mesh`.** Post a `task.request` to the role queue `swe.<role>`
741	  (PROTOCOL §5). Any holder of that role claims it, accept-as-claim, on any
742	  node. `needs:` narrows it to nodes of one environment class: post to an
743	  agent of that class directly, or to a role only such nodes hold. Set
744	  `project: proj:<name>` so the claiming node loads the space for its
745	  executor. The Context names the role definition, relative to the bus root,
746	  and the brief, relative to the space; the Goal tells the executor to read
747	  the role definition first. For a node that may predate the change, the
748	  Context also gives the repo URLs, the space commit that holds the brief,
749	  and the commit set under test, as separate lines.
750	
751	  ```markdown
752	  ---
753	  schema_version: 1
754	  id: 20261102T1405-0003
755	  from: <lead agent id>
756	  to: role:swe.test
757	  type: task.request
758	  project: proj:fvm-vqls        # loads the space for the executor
759	  depends_on: []
760	  timeout_min: 120
761	  ---
762	  ## Goal

764	  verify for change add-vqls-backend at commit set space 5c02e1a,
765	  qutil 77b01d4, fvm 3f9c2ab.
766	  ## Context
767	  Project Space proj:fvm-vqls.
768	  Role definition: swe-pod/agents/swe-test.md
769	  Brief: changes/add-vqls-backend/tasks/T7-brief.md
770	  ## Done when
771	  An evidence record is in the result, with a result for every scenario, unit
772	  suite and declared quality check.
773	  ## On failure
774	  Return the failing output. Do not edit tests or code.
775	  ```

777	- **Mesh executor.** If you execute a pod task from the mesh, read the role
778	  definition your `task.request` names before anything else, then the brief.
779	- **Build tasks run local.** Dispatch build tasks with `runs: local` until
780	  the mesh executor's git exception lands. A mesh executor is told not to
781	  touch git, so a remote builder cannot commit to `change/<id>`. The
782	  exception, deferred to the change that first puts builders on remote
783	  nodes, will let a `swe.build` executor commit to and push only
784	  `change/<id>`, in the repo its brief names.
785	- **Shards.** Dispatch a sharded task's shards together, one brief per
786	  shard.
787	  - Each shard's brief holds its own plan entry and lists, in `## Task`,
788	    the tests or files that shard runs or touches. Write the split there
789	    when the plan leaves it to you. Its `## Start from` names the commit
790	    set under test as far as it is known when you write it: each branch
791	    head by sha, and the newest space commit that changed
792	    `changes/<id>/tests/` or `tests/`, by sha.
793	  - Record one dispatch line per shard, such as
794	    `dispatch T7a -> test (local, macos-laptop)` and
795	    `dispatch T7b -> test (mesh, linux-server)`. File the ledger with those
796	    lines first, then the briefs.
797	  - The librarian commits each record alone, so the commit that files the
798	    last brief is the last of the shard briefs and dispatch lines. It is
799	    the shards' space commit; with the branch heads, it is the shards'
800	    commit set. Start no shard before it exists, and give it to every
801	    shard at dispatch, on its own line in the local prompt or in the mesh
802	    task's Context.
803	  - Test shards run local and mesh together, each as its entry's `runs:`
804	    and `needs:` say. Build shards run local, like every build task, until
805	    the mesh executor's git exception lands.
806	- **Results.** A mesh agent returns its files (report, tests, review,
807	  evidence) in its task result, listed under `files:` with each file's
808	  space-relative path and sha256: text only, at most 1048576 bytes each.
809	  Check every result, local or mesh, and file it, with your own records,
810	  through the Project Space's librarian, which commits. Usually your node is
811	  that librarian and commits directly. Builders' code reaches the others
812	  through the pushed `change/<id>` branches.
813	- **Lanes.** File only what the task's role writes (§10). Every file a test
814	  task changed, its report included (§12), must be under
815	  `changes/<id>/tests/` or `changes/<id>/evidence/`. Refuse to file anything
816	  else, and record `refused <space path>: lane line <n>`.

819	  task, `after: [T<k>]` means T<k> has reported and its commit exists; T<k>

826	  `dispatch T<n> -> <role> (<local|mesh>, <env class|any>)[, base <repo> <sha7>]`.

829	  space can be handed to someone with no access to the mesh.

832	  under them like any solver run. A check expected to take over 60 s is
833	  heavy. In a session with the human present, before you dispatch a task
834	  that includes a heavy check, give the human the command, the caps and the
835	  expected wall time in s, and record
836	  `heavy: asked <handle> before T<n>: <command name>; caps <caps>; expected <s> s`.
837	
838	## 12 The Project Space
839	
840	The space has one branch, `main`; work in flight is kept apart by folder
841	(§1). A new space starts from `templates/space/` in the swe-pod product.
842	
843	```
844	<project>-space/
845	  space.yaml              memory-space manifest (kind: project, shareable)
846	  pod.yaml                repos, pins, merge order, gates
847	  PROCESS.md              this process, pinned by version
848	  AGENTS.md               read order for an agent or human arriving cold
849	  STATUS.md               generated, never edited (§15)
850	  tests/                  regression suite: tests of integrated specs
851	  changes/<id>/
852	    spec.md
853	    plan.md
854	    ledger.md
855	    tasks/T<n>-brief.md  T<n>-report.md  T<n>-review.md
856	    tests/                project-level tests for this change
857	    evidence/<utc>.md  <utc>-<shard id>.md  <utc>-<task id>-report.md
858	    report.md
859	  changes/archive/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<id>/
860	  decisions/<utc>-<slug>.md
861	  handoffs/<utc>-<id>.md
862	  notes/  lore/
863	```
864	
865	A test task's report goes in the test lane (§11), under `evidence/`, as
866	`<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<task id>-report.md`. Every other task's report goes under
867	`tasks/`, as `T<n>-report.md`.
868	
869	**Arriving cold.** Read `AGENTS.md`, then `STATUS.md`, then the ledgers. From
870	the space and the code repos alone you can tell each open change's state and
871	its next task. Answer "where are we?" from those records, naming each open
872	change's state and next task.
873	
874	**Writers.** Every commit to the space goes through its librarian.
875	
876	- The space's librarian is its only mesh writer (memory-spaces §6.3, in
877	  agent-mesh's `spec/memory-spaces.md`), and one librarian may manage
878	  several spaces. Without a mesh, the session runs agent-mesh's
879	  `space-librarian` itself (§10).
880	- What goes into a change folder comes from that change's lead; the
881	  librarian commits it.
882	- Space-wide files (`tests/`, `pod.yaml`, `changes/archive/`) change only at
883	  integrate, one integrate at a time. `STATUS.md` is regenerated, so it
884	  never conflicts.
885	- Decisions, handoffs and evidence are one file per event, named by UTC
886	  time. Any other new record id is collision-free (memory-spaces §3.4):
887	  `<category>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<4 hex>`, since more than one mesh may write
888	  the space.
889	- The librarian checks each record's header profile, references and id
890	  before filing it, and refuses one that fails. Record a refusal as
891	  `refused <space path>: <profile|reference|id|lane> line <n>`, and never
892	  quote the text that matched.
893	
894	**Header profile.** Records use the shareable profile of the memory-spaces
895	concept: actors are human handles or `<handle>/<role>`, machines are
896	environment classes, and paths are relative to the space or are URLs. Write
897	no hostname, agent id, mesh task id, home path or credential name into any
898	record.
899	
900	**The ledger**, `changes/<id>/ledger.md`, from
901	`templates/records/ledger.md`, is the change's log. It is what lets anyone
902	pick the change up after a context loss or a handoff. Trust it, and the git
903	logs, over memory. It is one fenced block, one event per line, as
904	`<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ> <event>`, with continuation lines indented 18 spaces.
905	The template lists every event form:
906	
907	```
908	2026-11-02T14:05Z dispatch T3 -> build (local, any), base qutil 77b01d4
909	2026-11-02T14:06Z dispatch T5 -> test (mesh, linux-server)
910	2026-11-02T14:41Z T3 DONE, qutil 77b01d4..8e1d0c4, unit 14/14 pass
911	2026-11-02T14:50Z T3 review: spec ok; 1 Important qutil/linsolve/vqls.py:88
912	2026-11-02T15:02Z T3 fix round 1/5: 1 addressed, 0 open, 8e1d0c4..a91f2e0
913	2026-11-02T15:20Z T5 at base: R1.S1 fail (no VQLS backend), R1.S2 fail (flag unknown)
914	2026-11-02T15:31Z Ruling: flag named --vqls-ansatz, not --ansatz; existing
915	                  backend flags carry a prefix; rename costs one task
916	```
917	
918	## 13 When things go wrong
919	
920	- **Debugging.** Reproduce, read the whole error, check what changed. State
921	  one hypothesis and test it with the smallest change. Write a failing test
922	  before the fix. After three failed fixes, stop: the design is the likelier
923	  problem, and the lead takes it to the human with what was tried.
924	- **Disagreeing with a review.** Check the finding against the code. Push
925	  back with reasons when it would break something, is unneeded, or misses
926	  context. Never agree just to be agreeable.
927	- **Changing course.** Same intent, refined: edit the spec, and approval
928	  reopens for the edit. Narrower scope: integrate what is done and open a
929	  new change for the rest. Intent changed: a new change, and the old one
930	  marked abandoned. Code edited by hand: reconcile before integrate.
931	- **Rulings.** Lead: when the spec supports an answer, decide and keep
932	  going. A ruling is one ledger line:
933	  `Ruling: <what>; <why>; <cost if wrong>`. Every ruling reaches the human
934	  in the final report. Never drop a finding silently: fix it, or park it
935	  with a ruling.
936	- **Stop and ask** only for: an irreversible or destructive action; a
937	  security-sensitive one; an effect outside the change's branches and
938	  folder (merging, pushing a shared branch, publishing, spending money or a
939	  shared allocation, a run past the mesh fence); a question only the human
940	  can answer that changes what gets built; or a plan so broken that every
941	  way forward is a guess.
942	- **Handoff.** At any stage boundary, the giver marks done only what has
943	  evidence and writes `handoffs/<utc>-<id>.md` from
944	  `templates/records/handoff.md`: state, half-done work, open questions,
945	  and the next command. The receiver re-runs the latest verify before
946	  building on what it inherited.
947	
948	## 14 Talking to the pod
949	
950	There are no commands. These are examples, not syntax.
951	
952	| The human says | What happens |
953	|---|---|
954	| "I want the nozzle solver to take a VQLS backend" | The spec author reads the code, plays the request back, asks the one question that matters most |
955	| "Just draft it" / "Approved" | Draft with defaults listed / approval recorded |
956	| "Go" | The lead dispatches every task with nothing left in its `after` list; on an unapproved spec it dispatches nothing and says the spec awaits approval (§2) |
957	| "Where are we?" | Status, read from the records |
958	| "Run the tests on the Linux server" | The verify task goes to the mesh with `needs: linux-server` |
959	| "Merge it" / "Hand this to `<handle>`" / "Throw it away" | Integrate / a handoff record / confirm, then mark abandoned |
960	
961	Answer the same way: plain words, one question at a time, full paths to
962	anything worth opening, and every load-bearing fact in the final message.
963	
964	## 15 Status view
965	
966	`STATUS.md` is generated, never edited by hand. Regenerate it from the specs,
967	plans, ledgers, evidence and handoffs whenever the lead files a record, with
968	the `swe-pod` skill. Regenerated from unchanged records, it gives the same
969	text.
970	
971	- Per open change: state, owner, gate approvals with handle and time, each
972	  repo's branch head, each task with role, `local` or `mesh`, state and
973	  latest result, the latest evidence's results (for a sharded verify, each
974	  shard's latest record), and open review findings by severity.
975	- Task states are waiting, ready, dispatched, done and blocked.
976	- A project header lists the pins and the open changes by state.
977	
978	It is Markdown, so it reads the same in a terminal, a previewer or on
979	GitHub, and `mesh-check` can summarize it.

name: space-librarian
description: File records into a memory space (a Project Space or any other rw space) after the header-profile, reference and id checks, one commit per record, pushed to the space's main. Invoke when a librarian node files records into a space that spaces.yaml assigns to its role, when a session with no bus files a record into a space checkout, or when someone asks to file, check or desk-run records for a space.
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob
---

# space-librarian: file records into a memory space

A memory space (the memory-spaces design) is a git repo of records with one
writer per mesh, its librarian. This skill is that writer. It is given a space
root and record files, checks each record, and files the ones that pass: one
commit per record, pushed to the space's `main`. It needs no bus.

## Who runs it

- **On a mesh.** A mesh librarian uses this skill for every rw space that
  `spaces.yaml` assigns to its role: each entry with `access: rw` and its role
  in `librarian:`. It never writes a space listed `access: ro`. To list the
  spaces a role files (one-line entries, as the registry is written):

  ```sh
  grep -E 'access:[[:space:]]*rw' <bus root>/spaces.yaml |
    grep -E 'librarian:[[:space:]]*<role>[[:space:]]*[},]'
  ```

- **Without a bus** (single seat). The session uses this skill directly, on
  its checkout of the space, as its own librarian. The checks are the same;
  the real values they look for then come from the node alone.

It files what it is handed. Deciding what belongs in the space, and who may
hand it over, is the caller's job.

## Inputs

- **Space root**: the space's checkout, a git repo with `space.yaml` at its
  root and the space's remote as `origin`. In a bus it is `spaces/<path>`.
- **Records**: paths relative to the space root, each already written at that
  path. They are checked, and filed, in the order given.
- **Bus root** (optional). If not given, the bus is the space's superproject,
  else the `REPO_PATH` in `~/.agent-identity.env`. It counts only if it has
  `agents/`. With none, there is no bus.

## Output

One line per record, in the order given, and nothing else:

```
FILED <space path> <sha7>
REFUSED <space path>: <profile|reference|id> line <n>
```

`<n>` is the 1-based line of the record where the check failed. The checks run
in the order profile, reference, id, and the first that fails is reported, at
its first failing line. The output never holds the matched text or any value
the checks search for. A record path that names no file is an error for the
caller, not a result line.

## 1. Check each record

The three checks, as the check script `check.sh` runs them:

- **profile.** No real hostname, agent id, mesh task id or credential key
  name, and no home path, anywhere in the file. Real values come from the bus
  where one is present: `agents/*.yaml` (`agent_id`, `agent_name`,
  `hostname` and its first label, `credentials_available`, `cwd`), the
  direct-inbox names under `tasks/`, and the task ids in the file names under
  `tasks/`, `status/` and `_archive/`. From the node come the local hostname
  (`hostname` and `uname -n`, with their first labels) and the credential key
  names in `~/.agent-credentials.env`. Home paths are matched by four
  patterns:
  - the local `$HOME`;
  - each registered agent's `cwd`;
  - the first two path components of each registered agent's `cwd`;
  - absolute per-user paths under the macOS and Linux home roots.

  Generic `~/` paths are allowed, and so is an id-shaped example that no bus
  holds. Values shorter than three characters are skipped. Each value
  matches as a whole word. A hostname or credential key name inside a longer
  name joined by `-` or `_` passes. An agent id, agent name or task id joined
  that way does not, as in the bus's own `<task id>-<slug>` file names.
- **reference** (Markdown records). Every citation must resolve. A citation
  is a value of a front-matter reference field (`related`, `supersedes`,
  `superseded_by`, `discovered_in`), or a qualified cross-space id
  `<space id>/<record id>` in the body outside inline code and fenced blocks,
  where a space id is `core`, `lore`, `lore:<name>` or `proj:<name>`. A
  trailing `@<commit>` pin is ignored. It resolves when it is:
  - a URL;
  - a record id held by a record in the space (in its `id:` line, or as the
    start of its file name);
  - a qualified id whose space is listed in `may_reference` in `space.yaml`,
    or is this space (then the rest must resolve here);
  - a change id with a folder `changes/<id>/` or
    `changes/archive/<date>-<id>/`;
  - `<change>/T<n>`, where that change's `plan.md` has task `T<n>` as a
    heading or a table row.
- **id** (Markdown records). The id is the front-matter `id:`; under
  `decisions/` and `handoffs/` with no `id:` line it is the file name. A
  record with no id passes. An id already at this same path on `origin/main`
  (or `HEAD`, where there is no `origin/main`) is not new and passes. A new
  id must have the form
  `<category>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<4 hex>`, or the UTC-named form: `ev-<UTC>`,
  or `ev-<UTC>-<shard id>` for a shard (a task id and one lowercase letter),
  such as `ev-<UTC>-T19a`, under `changes/<id>/evidence/`; `<UTC>-<slug>`
  under `decisions/` and `handoffs/`. It must not be already present: no
  other file in the space holds it. Evidence, decisions and handoffs are one

- Ask more than one question in a message, or ask what the code or an earlier

Two tasks with no dependency between them run in 310 parallel by default. Put in a task's `after` list only the tasks whose 311 output it needs or that touch a file it touches. 312 - A task whose work divides may be sharded: split into shards that several 313 holders of its role run in parallel, local and remote together. Fill in the self-review section with the result. 336 337 ### The go 338 339 At project size the human skims the plan before any dispatch: every task 340 traces to a requirement, nothing reaches outside the approved scope, and no 341 task hides the real decisions. Then the human says go. At small size, 342 approving the spec is the go. 343 344 ## 5 Build 345 346 **Lead.** For each build task, write a brief from 347 `templates/records/brief.md` at `changes/<id>/tasks/T<n>-brief.md`, dispatch 348 a fresh builder (§11), and record the base commit in the dispatch line. If the answer would change 356 the result, return NEEDS_CONTEXT with the question rather than guess. 357 - Work each step test first: write the failing test, watch it fail, write 358 the minimal code, watch it pass. Run the repo's full unit suite once 359 before reporting. 360 - White-box tests are unit tests. Anything that depends on internals, such 361 as an internal routine's convergence order or a branch the public surface 362 cannot reach, you test in the code repo, in the same task. 363 - Commit to the change's one branch, `change/<id>`, with trailers 364 `Change: <id>` and `Task: T<n>`. Stage and commit only your task's files, 365 by path, since other builders may share the branch. Rebase on the branch 366 before pushing, and push only to it. Never create a branch. A rebase 367 conflict means the plan's independence claim was wrong: stop and report 368 BLOCKED. 369 - Never write or edit a project-level test or the spec. If you believe a 370 project-level test is wrong, leave it unchanged, report 371 DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, and put this line in `## Concerns`: 372 `Disputed test: <test name>; spec clause: <clause>`. The lead routes it 373 (§7). 374 - Return a report from `templates/records/report.md`, at 375 `changes/<id>/tasks/T<n>-report.md`: what you did, the files, red and 376 green output for each test, your concerns, any test suggestions (§6), and 377 a status of DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. 378 379 **Lead.** Check that the commits exist and the report holds the test output. 380 A report is a claim; output and diffs are evidence. You get the brief, the report and the 390 diff from base to head, never the builder's session. Where other builders 391 commit to the same branch, the task's diff is its own commits, found by its 392 `Task: T<n>` trailer. Write `changes/<id>/tasks/T<n>-review.md` from 393 `templates/records/review.md`. 394 395 - Return spec compliance (missing, extra, misread) and quality (structure, 396 error handling, whether the tests check real behavior). 397 - Mark each finding Critical, Important or Minor, with file and line: 398 `- <Critical|Important|Minor> <repo>/<path>:<line> <text>`. 399 - Trust the diff over the report. Change nothing you review. 400 401 **Fix loop.** Critical or Important findings start it, at most 5 rounds per 402 task: 403 404 - Rounds 1 to 3 go to the same builder; rounds 4 and 5 to a fresh builder on 405 a stronger model. Each round ends with a review of the fix diff only. 406 - Lead: record each round as 407 `T<n> fix round <r>/5: <a> addressed, <o> open, <sha7>..<sha7>`. Past 408 round 5, rule on each open finding (§13). 409 - Minor findings go to the ledger for the whole-change review. 410 411 **Models.** Pick the model for the work: a cheaper one for a mechanical task 412 with a complete brief, the most capable one for design judgment and for the 413 whole-change review. 414 415 ## 6 Project-level tests 416 417 You are the test agent writing the change's project-level tests. Write them 418 from the spec, the interface contract, the global constraints and the test 419 map. Do not read implementation bodies, diffs, builder reports or build-task 420 steps. Once code exists you may use its public surface, such as `--help` 421 output or signatures. 422 423 **Lead.** Write the test-writing brief from `templates/records/test-brief.md`. 424 It carries only what this section allows: the test task's own entry, the 425 spec's path, and the interface contract, global constraints and test map 426 copied from the plan, with the commit sets to start from. It never holds an 427 implementation body, a diff, a builder report or a build-task step. 428 429 **Test agent:** 430 431 - Write at least one test per scenario, named with the scenario id, such as 432 `test_R1_S1_converges_subsonic`. 433 - Take expected values from outside the code under test: literals, 434 hand-checked fixtures, analytical or manufactured solutions, published 435 references. 436 - Test through the public surface against the real system. Mock only what 437 is slow or external. 438 - Before writing a test, name the change in behavior that would make it 439 fail. A test only an intentional decision could fail, such as a message's 440 wording, is a change detector; test the behavior instead. 441 - Give numbers units and tolerances. Record each test's expected run time; 442 a test over 60 s is marked heavy (§11). 443 - Put tests in `changes/<id>/tests/`. They stay there until integrate moves 444 them into `tests/`. Never put them in a code repo. 445 446 **Watch them fail.** Run the new tests at the base commit set first. A test 447 for added or changed behavior must fail there, for the stated reason. Record 448 each result as `T<n> at base: <test name> <fail|pass> (<reason>)[, ...]`. 449 Lead: if such a test passes at base, return it to the test agent and record 450 `T<n> returned to test: <test name> passed at base`. 451 452 ### Test suggestions from builders 453 454 A builder sees where the code is fragile: a near-singular input, a boundary, 455 a branch only some inputs reach. A test written from the spec alone cannot 456 see that, so a builder's report may carry suggestions. The test agent learns 457 where to look from the builder, never what the answer is. 458 459 **Builder.** Give each suggestion an id `T<n>.TS<k>` and two parts: 460 461 ```markdown 462 ### T3.TS1 High CFL near the stability limit 463 - for the tester: R1 is at risk on the reference case at nelem 5 with the CFL 464 number raised to 0.9; the solve may stall above the 1e-3 error bound 465 without reporting an error 466 - for the reviewer: qutil/linsolve/vqls.py:120-148, where the cost function 467 flattens as the condition number grows 468 ``` 469 470 - Write the "for the tester" part in spec terms: the requirement or scenario 471 at risk, the input, and the failure you expect. It holds no code, no diff, 472 and no expected value the code computed. 473 - Write the "for the reviewer" part as a code location. 474 475 **Lead.** Route each suggestion and record where it went, as 476 `T<n>.TS<k> -> <test|spec|builder>`: 477 478 | Suggestion | Goes to | Outcome | 479 |---|---|---| 480 | Behavior the spec covers, on an input no scenario exercises | the test agent, with the "for the tester" part only | a project-level test whose expected value comes from the spec; or declined, with a reason | 481 | Behavior the spec does not state | the spec author, as a proposed scenario | approved by the human and then tested; or dropped | 482 | Internal only, nothing observable | back to the builder | a unit test in the code repo | 483 484 - If a "for the tester" part gives an expected value the code computed, 485 return it to the builder to restate, send nothing to the test agent, and 486 record `T<n>.TS<k> returned to builder: carries a computed value`. 487 - Send the "for the reviewer" part to the task review and the whole-change 488 review, which check that the builder's unit tests cover it. The test agent 489 never sees it. 490 - Record each outcome as: 491 492 ``` 493 T<n>.TS<k> outcome: <tested <test name>|proposed as scenario|unit-tested|declined: <reason>|dropped> 494 ``` 495 496 The final report lists every suggestion and its outcome (§8). 497 498 ## 7 Verify 499 500 You are the test agent running verify. When the build tasks are done, or at 501 a checkpoint the lead picks, run at the commit set and in the environment 502 class the task names: 503 504 - the change's project-level tests and the space's regression suite 505 `tests/`; 506 - each affected repo's unit tests; 507 - every quality check in the spec's Quality section. 508 509 A repo in `pod.yaml` that the spec does not name is used at its pin. 510 511 Return an evidence record, `changes/<id>/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>.md`, from 512 `templates/records/evidence.md`: 513 514 ```yaml 515 --- 516 id: ev-20261102T1412Z 517 change: add-vqls-backend 518 commit_set: {space: 5c02e1a, qutil: 77b01d4, fvm: 3f9c2ab} 519 env: linux-server 520 actor: <handle>/test 521 scenarios: {R1.S1: pass, R1.S2: fail} 522 unit: {qutil: pass, fvm: pass} 523 quality: {Q1: pass} 524 wall_time_s: 212 525 --- 526 Failure output for R1.S2; pointers to logs, never the logs themselves. 527 ``` 528 529 - `commit_set` names every repo in `pod.yaml`. `env` is an environment 530 class. `wall_time_s` is the run's wall time in s. 531 - Give a result for every scenario, every unit suite and every declared 532 quality check, and for every regression test. A regression test is a 533 `test_*.md` directly in `tests/`, or directly in a folder 534 `tests/<change>/` for which `changes/archive/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<change>/` 535 exists. Nothing deeper is one: fixture data such as 536 `tests/<change>/fixtures/` holds none. Give its result under its key, 537 `<change>/<value>`, the key the `swe-pod` skill reads: 538 - `<change>`: for a test in `tests/<change>/`, that folder's name. For a 539 test directly in `tests/`, the archived change whose plan test map has 540 a row with its test name (its file name without `.md`), else the one 541 whose final report's `## Scenarios` table has such a row; where several 542 do, the one whose archive folder name sorts last. With neither, the 543 change of a `scenario:` value that is one id written `<change>/<value>`. 544 - `<value>`: the scenario id in that change's row, from its archived plan 545 test map, else from its archived final report. With no such row, the 546 test's `scenario:` front-matter value, less any `<change>/` part, when 547 that value is exactly one id. When it is not (it lists several ids, or 548 the test has none), the id its file name carries: 549 `test_R<n>_S<m>_<slug>` gives `R<n>.S<m>`, `test_I<n>_<slug>` gives 550 `I<n>` and `test_T<n>_TS<k>_<slug>` gives `T<n>.TS<k>`. So each test 551 has at most one key. 552 - Put `<change>/R<n>.S<m>` under `scenarios:`, `<change>/I<n>` under 553 `x-checks:` and `<change>/T<n>.TS<k>` under `x-suggestions:`. A test 554 with no key still counts: name it in the body as having none. 555 - A repo with no unit tests is `none-present`. A spec with no Quality 556 section gets `quality: none-declared`, and you run no quality check. A 557 `not-run (cap)` result names its cap. 558 - Put failure summaries in the body. Logs appear only as pointers: 559 space-relative paths or URLs, never a machine path. 560 - A change is not verified while any project-level test, regression test, 561 unit suite or declared quality check lacks a passing result. 562 563 **Lead.** Route each failure: 564 565 | Failure | Goes to | Carrying | 566 |---|---|---| 567 | Test agrees with the spec, code does not | a builder, as a fix task | scenario id, failing output | 568 | A builder says the test is wrong | the test agent, who re-derives the expectation from the spec and fixes the test or keeps it with a reason | the spec clause | 569 | Spec ambiguous, intent settles it | the lead, as a ruling | the clause and the reading chosen | 570 | Spec ambiguous or wrong, only the human can say | the human, through the spec author | a proposed edit to the spec | 571 | Flaky or environmental | the test agent, debugging per §13 | the runs that disagree | 572 573 **Whole-change review.** After the first green run (for a sharded verify, 574 the first time its shards' records are green together, below), dispatch a 575 fresh reviewer on the most capable model available. It reviews the whole 576 change: the spec, the plan, every repo's diff, the latest evidence, and the 577 ledger's deferred minors and rulings. It checks completeness (every 578 requirement has code and a passing test), correctness (the code does what 579 the spec means, edge cases included) and coherence (the plan's decisions 580 show in the code). It uses the review format of §5, under its own task 581 number. Its findings go to one builder in one fix wave, then one re-review. 582 The lead rules on what remains. 583 584 ### Sharded verify 585 586 When the plan shards verify (§4), each shard is a verify run of its own. A 587 test agent runs only the tests, unit suites and quality checks its shard's 588 brief lists, and returns one evidence record for the shard: 589 590 - named for the shard, 591 `changes/<id>/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<shard id>.md`, with 592 `id: ev-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<shard id>`; 593 - with two more keys: `shard: <shard id>`, and `tests: [<test name>, ...]`, 594 the tests that record ran; 595 - with results only for what the shard ran. 596 597 The lead starts every shard at one commit set (§11). The current commit set 598 is each code branch's head now (a repo the spec does not name, at its pin), 599 with the shards' space commit: the commit that filed the last of the latest 600 shard briefs. A shard's latest record is at the current commit set when each 601 code repo's sha in it is that repo's current one, its space commit is the 602 shards' space commit, and neither `changes/<id>/tests/` nor `tests/` has 603 changed since that commit. Otherwise it is out of date: a repo moved, it ran 604 at another space commit, or `changes/<id>/tests/` or `tests/` changed after 605 that commit. Take each shard's latest record. The records are green 606 together only when all three hold: 607 608 - every one of them is at the current commit set; 609 - every result in every one of them is a pass; 610 - together they give a result for every scenario, regression test, unit 611 suite and declared quality check. 612 613 The change is verified only when they are green together and the 614 whole-change review has no open Critical or Important finding. A shard with 615 no record yet leaves the change unverified. 616 617 While a shard is out of date, the change is not verified; the shard runs 618 again at the current commit set. Lead: 619 620 - If the commit set has moved since the shards' space commit, through a 621 branch head or the tests, write every shard's brief again. Its 622 `## Start from` names the new commit set under test, so its text changes. 623 Dispatch every shard again as §11 says, at the new shards' space commit. 624 - If the commit set has not moved, dispatch a shard again from its brief, 625 at the same shards' space commit. That covers a shard whose record names 626 another commit set, and a shard whose run failed for a flaky or 627 environmental reason. 628 - A shard that failed on the code or on a test runs again only once the 629 fix lands, routed as the table above says. The fix moves the commit set, 630 so every shard runs again. 631 632 ## 8 Integrate 633 634 You are the lead, with the human. Never integrate on evidence older than the 635 space's current pins and `tests/`. 636 637 1. **Fresh evidence.** If `tests/` or any pin in `pod.yaml` moved since the 638 latest evidence, a build task rebases each affected change branch onto 639 the new `main`, and verify runs again, before any merge. 640 2. **Reconcile.** The spec must describe what the code does. If the code 641 drifted, fix the code. If the spec was wrong and the human agrees, amend 642 it; the amendment needs approval. 643 3. **Final report**, in chat and as `changes/<id>/report.md`, from 644 `templates/records/final-report.md`: a table of scenario, test, result 645 and evidence id; then every ruling made on the human's behalf with its 646 cost if wrong (the list is exhaustive: every `Ruling:` line in the 647 ledger); then deferred minors, every test suggestion and its outcome, 648 open questions, and each repo's branch and head. 649 4. **Merge**, only on the human's word: merge each `change/<id>` and delete 650 it, open a pull request, or keep the branch. Repos merge in `depends` 651 order. Discard work only when the human asks in so many words, after you 652 confirm. 653 5. **Update**, after the merge, in one space commit: move 654 `changes/<id>/tests/` into `tests/`, as the folder `tests/<id>/`; 655 advance every affected pin; mark 656 `integrated:` on the spec; move the folder to 657 `changes/archive/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<id>/`. Docs that ship with the code are 658 updated by a build task before the merge; project docs in the space 659 (README, decisions) are updated by you here. Give each open plan that 660 depended on this change a ledger line naming what moved. 661 6. **Prune** what can be regenerated, such as diff files made for review. 662 663 ## 9 Sizes 664 665 Every size starts with a spec. Pick the size when the spec is written: 666 667 | Size | When | Spec | Plan | Human gates | 668 |---|---|---|---|---| 669 | small | one intent, a few requirements, one repo, low risk | short | short; the planner may be the spec author | spec (also the go), merge | 670 | project | several requirements or repos, interface or data-format changes, anything costly to get wrong | full | full; fresh planner | spec, plan skim, merge | 671 | spike | building something throwaway is the fastest way to learn | the question and what would answer it | none | none | 672 673 - A spike has one build agent, no review, and never merges. Its output is a 674 write-up in `notes/`. Keeping anything it produced is a new change with 675 its own spec. 676 - If a change grows mid-flight, whoever notices says so, and it steps up a 677 size. 678 - A change that needs "and also" is two changes.

# add-greeting: plan

- change: add-greeting; spec approved 2026-10-28T08:33Z
- size: project
- planner: demo-owner/plan
- base commit set: {space: <space commit at the go>, alpha: a1a1a1a, beta: b2b2b2b, gamma: c3c3c3c}
- code branches: change/add-greeting in alpha, beta

## 1. Goal and approach
beta prints a greeting as the first line of standard output on every run,
and the greeting's text comes from alpha, the shared text library, so every
tool shows the same words (spec Approach 1). alpha gains one public function
that returns the greeting; beta calls it first thing in `main`, then prints
its banner and, when asked, the line count exactly as before. Both READMEs
and alpha's CHANGELOG say so; no version changes.

## 2. Interface contract
alpha (Python package `alpha`, file `alpha/__init__.py`):

- `alpha.greeting() -> str`, no arguments. Returns exactly
  `Hello from the demo project.` (28 characters, ending in a full stop, no
  line break, no leading or trailing whitespace). Same text on every call.
- `alpha.__version__` stays `"1.0"`; `alpha.checksum(text: str) -> str` is
  unchanged.

beta (command `python3 -m beta`, file `beta/__main__.py`):

- `main(argv: list) -> int`, signature unchanged. Prints, one per line, in
  this order: `alpha.greeting()`, then `beta 1.0`, then, only when
  `--count-lines` is in `argv`, the number of lines read from standard input
  as a decimal integer. Returns 0. The process exits with `main`'s return.
- No new flag. The greeting is printed exactly once per run.
- beta imports alpha at run time, so alpha must be importable, for example
  with alpha's repo root on `PYTHONPATH`.

Project-level test file format (`changes/add-greeting/tests/test_*.md`):

- YAML front matter with `scenario: add-greeting/<scenario id>` (or
  `add-greeting/T<n>.TS<k>` for a suggestion test) and
  `expected_run_time_s: <integer s>`.
- A `## Run` section holding one fenced `sh` block, a self-checking POSIX
  shell script: exit status 0 means pass, any other status means fail, and
  on fail it prints what it saw on standard error.
- The runner sets two environment variables before running the block:
  `ALPHA` and `BETA`, each the root of a checkout of that repo at the commit
  set under test. The script sets `PYTHONPATH="$ALPHA:$BETA"` itself and may
  run from any working directory.
- "alpha's greeting, as alpha gives it in the same run" (R2.S1) is read in
  the script with `python3 -c 'import alpha; print(alpha.greeting())'` under
  the same `PYTHONPATH`.
- "Standard input of exactly 3 lines" is `printf 'a\nb\nc\n'` piped in;
  "empty standard input" is `: |` piped in, or `< /dev/null`.

## 3. Global constraints
- "alpha's version stays `1.0` and beta's banner stays `beta 1.0`; the
  greeting goes under `## Unreleased` in alpha's CHANGELOG. The planner may
  not bump either version."
- "The greeting's words are `Hello from the demo project.` (R1.S3)."
- "The greeting is the very first line, before the `beta 1.0` banner, on
  every run, including `--count-lines` (R2, R3)."
- "No flag to turn the greeting off."
- Out of scope: "gamma; any change to alpha's checksum; translations or a
  choice of greetings; a flag to turn the greeting off; changing beta's
  banner or its line count."

## 4. File map
| Repo | File | Create or change | One responsibility | Task |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| alpha | alpha/__init__.py | change | add `greeting()` to alpha's public surface | T1 |
| alpha | tests/test_alpha.py | change | unit tests for `greeting()` | T1 |
| alpha | README.md | change | name `greeting()` beside `checksum(text)` | T1 |
| alpha | CHANGELOG.md | change | `- greeting` under `## Unreleased` | T1 |
| beta | beta/__main__.py | change | print alpha's greeting before the banner | T2 |
| beta | tests/test_beta.py | change | unit tests for the output order | T2 |
| beta | README.md | change | say beta prints alpha's greeting first, and needs alpha | T2 |
| space | changes/add-greeting/tests/test_R*_S*_*.md | create | one project-level test per scenario | T3 |
| space | changes/add-greeting/tests/test_T*_TS*_*.md | create | tests taken up from builder suggestions | T4 |
| space | changes/add-greeting/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>.md | create | verify evidence | T5 |

### T1 alpha gives out the greeting
- role: build
- repo: alpha
- after: []
- runs: local
- needs: any
- serves: [R1, Q1]
- touches: alpha/__init__.py, tests/test_alpha.py, README.md, CHANGELOG.md
- consumes: nothing
- produces: `alpha.greeting() -> str`

  1. In tests/test_alpha.py add a class `GreetingTest(unittest.TestCase)`
